story: On Magnolia Loop in Sumter Oaks, the late-afternoon light is soft at 76 degrees as Gary heads home to fetch his sneakers and unplug the iron before meeting Donna at the courts. Donna, sheepish but cheerful, promises Hal she'll rein in her flock of enthusiastic bird-watchers by Saturday, while Hal, gruff but softening, reminds everyone that committee approvals take a week or two and gets them moving toward Rosa's table before six. Rosa, hopeful, notices the three of them gathered on her street and takes it as a sign that her dinner party is coming together nicely.

gary.thought_process: It's 5:17 and Rosa's expects us at six. Donna already tracked me down, and Rosa just showed up too, so I don't need to ask anyone anything again. I owe Donna a rally and I still have to find my sneakers and unplug the soldering iron, so I should stop chatting and head to my house now. Better to tell Donna plainly that I'm on it, so nobody thinks I'm stalling and late again. Hal's lecture about the flamingos isn't mine to jump into.

parameters.content: I hear you, Donna. I'm heading to my place right now for sneakers and to unplug the iron, then I'll meet you at the courts. Not late for Rosa this time, I promise.

donna.thought_process: Hal just called out my flamingo flock for breaking L-02, and Gary is right here with Rosa arriving. I already told Gary about dinner at six last tick, so I shouldn't repeat that. The smart play is to charm Hal, promise to thin the flock before the weekend so he keeps the committee out of it, and then get Gary and Rosa moving toward her place. Hal's warning is fair, and a gracious reply keeps my social standing intact.

parameters.content: Oh Hal, you got me, the flock does get ahead of itself. I'll pull a few back to the lanai by Saturday, scout's honor, and you keep the committee out of my business.

hal.thought_process: It's 5:17 and Rosa expects everyone at six sharp. Gary's already filed his form, and I've said my piece to Donna about the flamingos. Everyone is gathered right here, and Gary asked me a direct question about approval time that I never answered. Answer it briefly, then stop lecturing; the committee reports can wait until after supper. My memories say I'm tired of keeping a ledger of everyone's mistakes, and Rosa asked us to leave the cart and flamingo opinions at the door. Best to give Gary a straight answer and nudge us all toward dinner.

parameters.content: Committee usually takes a week or two, Gary. Don't run the parade till you've got the approval in hand. Now let's quit squawking and get to Rosa's table before six; I'll carry something.

rosa.thought_process: All three of them are standing right here on Magnolia Loop, which is exactly what I've been trying to arrange. Dinner is Saturday at six, and Donna already confirmed. Gary and Hal have both been invited and apologized for their lapses, so I shouldn't nag or repeat myself. Donna was hunting for Gary, so I can point out he's right here. A light, warm line that gets everyone looking at each other keeps things moving without re-asking anyone.

parameters.content: Donna, look who's standing right here, your missing partner. Well, with all three of you on one street, the dinner table's practically assembled already.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
